reason: A provides the more physically plausible and testable mechanism: systematically varying FCC/BCC interphase-boundary density and measuring creep rate, strain partitioning, and dislocation structures directly tests interface-controlled creep resistance within a defined dislocation-creep regime. B assumes naturally coherent FCC/BCC interfaces without evidence, uses annealing that strongly confounds coherency with phase fraction and coarsening, and places the test below ~0.4 Tm where measurable high-temperature creep may be limited.
